newsitem.title: UK: FedEx eyes 10 A3XX freighters - Airbus.
newsitem.headline: FedEx eyes 10 A3XX freighters - Airbus.

text.p: Federal Express Corp has expressed interest in acquiring "approximately 10" Airbus Industrie A3XX freighters, John Leahy, a senior vice-president at the European manufacturer, said.
He said that the cost of each of the proposed long-range aircraft, was $198 million per plane.
Leahy told Reuters that FedEx had played a pivotal role in forming an A3XX cargo working group with Airbus.

The first meeting of this group -- one of up to 10 formed by Airbus to focus on A3XX-related matters -- was held in Memphis at the instigation of the U.S. freight integrator's chairman Fred Smith two months ago and was attended by 12 airlines, Leahy said.
He said he expected the next meeting of the cargo group to take place in the near future, although he was unable to give exact dates or the venue.
Smith said on January 29 that FedEx was not just looking at an aircraft that was marginally bigger than its McDonnell Douglas MD-11 freighters, which can each uplift around 65 tonnes of freight.
The four-engined A3XX freighter, if the project gets the go-ahead, would be one-third larger than a Boeing 747 freighter and able to carry some 130 tonnes of cargo, said Leahy.
He earlier told a news conference here that the A3XX development programme would cost $8 billion, 40 percent of which was expected to come from risk-sharing partners outside the Airbus consortium.
"I don't think there will be any problem in raising the $8 billion," he said, adding that risk-sharing partners were being sought in Asia, Europe and North America.

Leahy added that a final decision on whether or not to go ahead with the A3XX project would be taken in December 1998. If approval is given, he expected the first aircraft to be flying in 2003, with engines provided either by Rolls-Royce or a Pratt & Whitney /General Electric Co joint venture.
Leahy said that although some A3XX freighter sales were anticipated, he expected the greater proportion of future freighters would be conversions from passenger aircraft.
Airbus Industrie's vice-president for strategic planning, Adam Brown, forecast that during the next 20 years, 74 airlines would need 1,440 aircraft in size categories above the 747-400.

Airbus is a consortium made up of French state-owned Ste Nationale Industrielle Aerospatiale, British Aerospace Plc, Daimler-Benz Aerospace, a unit of Daimler-Benz AG and Construcciones Aeronauticas SA(CASA) of Spain)
